sections.body: Sexual and reproductive health is about wellbeing, safety and making informed choices. Laws on age of consent and access to services differ by country. Know your local laws and services.
Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) can often have no symptoms. Condoms reduce the risk of many STIs. Testing is confidential in many places.
Contraception methods (such as condoms, the pill and implants) help prevent pregnancy. Doctors and sexual health clinics can explain options.
Reliable sources: doctors, school nurses, official health services and WHO. Pornography is not sex education. It often shows unrealistic and non-consensual behaviour.

quiz.q: Can someone have an STI without any symptoms?
options: Yes, many STIs can have no symptoms
hints: The lesson says something about symptoms.
Some illnesses, like high blood pressure, often have no obvious signs, so checks are needed.
quiz.explain: Yes. Many STIs have no symptoms, which is why testing matters.

quiz.q: Where is the most reliable place to get sexual health information?
options: A doctor, nurse or official health service
hints: For a broken arm you'd see a doctor, not a random video. Sexual health is the same.
quiz.explain: Doctors, nurses and official health services give accurate, confidential advice.

quiz.q: Which method helps prevent pregnancy AND reduces the risk of many STIs?
hints: The lesson lists several contraception methods, but only one also appears in the section about STIs.
STIs pass from person to person through sexual contact. Which option is a physical barrier between people, rather than a method that works inside one person's body?

Worked example: the HPV vaccine protects against certain types of one infection (HPV), but it doesn't prevent pregnancy. Each method protects against different things, so check what each one actually does.
quiz.explain: Condoms are a barrier method: they help prevent pregnancy and reduce the risk of many STIs. The pill and implants are effective at preventing pregnancy but don't protect against STIs. A doctor or sexual health clinic can explain the options.
